title: How Alignment Services & Plans Holdings End: Expiration and Vehicle Retirement
content:
An Alignment Services & Plans holding ends without a refund in two ways, and the plan must be in status active when it ends, as its own system record shows.

1. **Expiration.** A month-based plan or single service expires the day after its expiration date.
2. **Vehicle retirement.** Any plan ends as vehicle retired on the date Crestline records that the purchaser no longer owns the vehicle — the vehicle is no longer on the purchaser's profile, or the customer reports the sale. Because no holding can move to another vehicle or owner and every holding ends when the purchaser no longer owns the vehicle, the plan never moves to the buyer or to the purchaser's replacement vehicle.

A readjustment owed on an alignment performed before the end remains available under the readjustment guarantee.

### Cases (hypothetical)
| Situation | How the holding ends |
|---|---|
| 1-Year plan with an expiration date of 30 June | expires on 1 July, no refund |
| Lifetime plan; the customer reports selling the car | ends as vehicle retired on the date recorded, no refund |
| Lifetime plan; the vehicle no longer appears on the purchaser's profile | ends as vehicle retired on the date recorded, no refund |
| Plan already cancelled | it is not in status active, so neither ending applies |
